topic: The Mystery of Pi in the Normal Distribution

sections.title: The Hook: The Gaussian Bell Curve
lecture_lines: The Gaussian function defines the bell curve.
The normalization constant ensures total area is one.
Why does π appear in the constant?
animations: Create a Normal Distribution curve centered at zero (#FFD700) and place the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bell.svg] icon at the center.
Label the vertical peak as 1 over root 2π (#FFFFFF).
Highlight the area under the curve in blue (#00BFFF).

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Gaussian Integral
lecture_lines: To find C, integrate e to minus x squared.
The integral has no elementary antiderivative.
We need a clever way to compute it.
animations: Show Gaussian function f(x) = e^-x^2 on screen (#FFFFFF) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg].
Fade in integral from negative to positive infinity (#FFD700).
Display final result as square root of π (#00FF00) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg].

sections.title: The Coordinate Transformation Trick
lecture_lines: Square the integral for a 2D surface.
Transition from Cartesian to polar coordinates.
Polar coordinates naturally involve circles and π.
animations: Create two identical Gaussian integrals in x and y (#FFFFFF) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/protractor.svg].
Transform the pair into polar coordinates (r, θ) (#FFD700).
Show the Jacobian r dr dθ conversion clearly (#00BFFF) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg].

sections.title: The Emergence of π
lecture_lines: Integrating over dθ from zero to 2π.
animations: Simplify the polar integral expression to 2π times integral (#FFFFFF) using the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg].
Evaluate the inner integral to reveal a constant (#FFD700).
Conclude the value is π by cancelling factors (#00FF00) as shown on the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/globe.svg].

sections.title: Conclusion: The Geometric Bridge
lecture_lines: The 1D curve is a simple slice.
Geometry and probability bridge through π.
animations: Connect probability theory to circular geometry concepts using a protractor [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/protractor.svg] (#FFFFFF).
Show how π naturally appears in normal distributions (#FFD700).
Summarize the bridge between algebra and circles [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bridge.svg] (#00BFFF).
